python3 << 'EOF'
import json

# Data for FY 1991-2010 (all in millions of dollars)
# Source: Treasury Bulletin September 1996, 2001, 2006, 2011
data = {
    1991: {"on_budget": 760375, "off_budget": 293885},  # 1996 bulletin
    1992: {"on_budget": 789266, "off_budget": 302426},  # 1996 bulletin
    1993: {"on_budget": 841241, "off_budget": 311934},  # 1996 bulletin
    1994: {"on_budget": 922161, "off_budget": 335026},  # 1996 bulletin
    1995: {"on_budget": 999496, "off_budget": 351080},  # 1996 bulletin
    1996: {"on_budget": 1085271, "off_budget": 367492}, # 2001 bulletin
    1997: {"on_budget": 1186987, "off_budget": 391989}, # 2001 bulletin
    1998: {"on_budget": 1305621, "off_budget": 415800}, # 2001 bulletin
    1999: {"on_budget": 1382834, "off_budget": 444468}, # 2001 bulletin
    2000: {"on_budget": 1544455, "off_budget": 480583}, # 2001 bulletin
    2001: {"on_budget": 1483525, "off_budget": 507519}, # 2006 bulletin
    2002: {"on_budget": 1337730, "off_budget": 515321}, # 2006 bulletin
    2003: {"on_budget": 1258265, "off_budget": 523842}, # 2006 bulletin
    2004: {"on_budget": 1345040, "off_budget": 534744}, # 2006 bulletin
    2005: {"on_budget": 1575874, "off_budget": 577475}, # 2006 bulletin
    2006: {"on_budget": 1797946, "off_budget": 608382}, # 2011 bulletin
    2007: {"on_budget": 1932359, "off_budget": 635088}, # 2011 bulletin
    2008: {"on_budget": 1865279, "off_budget": 658045}, # 2011 bulletin
    2009: {"on_budget": 1450355, "off_budget": 654010}, # 2011 bulletin
    2010: {"on_budget": 1530058, "off_budget": 631688}, # 2011 bulletin
}

# Extract X (on-budget) and Y (off-budget) values
on_budget = [data[year]["on_budget"] for year in range(1991, 2011)]
off_budget = [data[year]["off_budget"] for year in range(1991, 2011)]

print("On-budget receipts (millions $):", on_budget)
print("Off-budget receipts (millions $):", off_budget)
print()

# Calculate R-squared using simple linear regression
# X = on-budget, Y = off-budget
# R^2 = correlation coefficient squared

import statistics

# Calculate means
mean_x = statistics.mean(on_budget)
mean_y = statistics.mean(off_budget)

# Calculate correlation coefficient
def pearson_correlation(x, y):
    n = len(x)
    mean_x = sum(x) / n
    mean_y = sum(y) / n
    
    numerator = sum((x[i] - mean_x) * (y[i] - mean_y) for i in range(n))
    denominator_x = sum((x[i] - mean_x) ** 2 for i in range(n)) ** 0.5
    denominator_y = sum((y[i] - mean_y) ** 2 for i in range(n)) ** 0.5
    
    return numerator / (denominator_x * denominator_y)

correlation = pearson_correlation(on_budget, off_budget)
r_squared = correlation ** 2

print(f"Mean on-budget: {mean_x:,.2f}")
print(f"Mean off-budget: {mean_y:,.2f}")
print(f"Pearson correlation: {correlation:.10f}")
print(f"R-squared: {r_squared:.10f}")
print(f"R-squared (rounded to 4 decimal places): {round(r_squared, 4)}")
EOF
